name: GCP Credential Theft from gcloud Config (disk)
description: On a compromised host with the gcloud SDK, harvest cached credentials from the gcloud config directory: OAuth access/refresh tokens (access_tokens.db, credentials.db), legacy SA keys (legacy_credentials/), and Application Default Credentials. These let you re-authenticate as the host's user/SA from your own machine.
source: MCRTA (CyberWarFare Labs) - Multi-Cloud Red Team Analyst: GCP

examples.label: Dump cached OAuth tokens
examples.command:
sqlite3 ~/.config/gcloud/access_tokens.db 'select account_id,access_token,token_expiry from access_tokens;'
sqlite3 ~/.config/gcloud/credentials.db 'select account_id,value from credentials;'

examples.label: Reuse a stolen token / refresh creds on your box

notes: gcloud caches credentials in the config dir (CLOUDSDK_CONFIG; default ~/.config/gcloud on *nix, %APPDATA%\gcloud on Windows). Loot: access_tokens.db (table access_tokens: account_id, access_token, token_expiry, rapt_token) - short-lived but immediately usable; credentials.db (table credentials: account_id, value) - contains refresh tokens = long-lived re-auth; legacy_credentials/<account>/ - older SA key material; application_default_credentials.json - ADC used by SDKs. Refresh tokens are the prize (persistent). Copy the whole gcloud dir to your box (set CLOUDSDK_CONFIG to it) to inherit the victim's sessions. Classic on any dev/CI host with gcloud installed.

recommended.note: Enumerate what the stolen identity can do

defense.why_it_works: The gcloud SDK caches OAuth access and refresh tokens (SQLite DBs), legacy SA keys, and Application Default Credentials in a predictable, user-readable config directory. Anyone with access to that user's files can copy the tokens/keys and re-authenticate as the identity from anywhere - refresh tokens give durable access.
defense.prerequisites: File access on a host with gcloud configured (developer workstation, CI runner, jump box) - as the user or root.
defense.impact: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files + T1528 Steal Application Access Token. Re-authentication as the host's GCP user/SA off-host; refresh tokens = persistent access.
defense.detection: Cloud Audit Logs: the user's token used from a new IP/user agent shortly after host compromise; impossible travel. Endpoint: processes reading ~/.config/gcloud/*.db or copying the gcloud dir; sqlite access to access_tokens.db/credentials.db.
defense.artifacts: EDR/file-access telemetry on the gcloud config dir; audit-log sign-ins of the stolen identity from attacker infrastructure.
defense.prevention: Avoid standing gcloud logins on shared/CI hosts - use short-lived Workload Identity Federation / attached SAs. Protect and monitor the config dir; use OS credential protection. Enable context-aware access so tokens are bound to trusted devices/IPs. Rotate/revoke on host compromise (gcloud auth revoke; revoke refresh tokens).
defense.evasion: Reuse the token/refresh cred from an IP/region near the victim; import into your gcloud (CLOUDSDK_CONFIG) so calls mimic the user's normal usage.
defense.misconfiguration: Long-lived gcloud logins/refresh tokens on shared or internet-exposed hosts; no context-aware access binding tokens to devices.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Any local file access yields reusable creds:
cp -r ~/.config/gcloud /tmp/exfil   # refresh tokens + ADC + legacy keys
